gold_decisions.identity_explanation: The gold issue concerns an unsupported general second-order convergence guarantee for the entire numerical scheme versus a narrower integral-discretization result. ISSUE-002 instead diagnoses that one parameter set violates the framework's finite-variance assumption; it does not identify the missing full-scheme convergence argument or the mismatch in convergence object and rate.

The gold issue is the missing density-variation or derivative control needed for the weighted midpoint cancellation and convergence estimate. ISSUE-002 concerns the separate condition B_ell>2 and whether VG0 belongs to the finite-variance framework; it provides no diagnosis of rough-density oscillation, first-variation control, or the weighted midpoint estimate.

Both issues involve formulas containing rho, but the gold defect is that the active positive-semidefinite assumption permits singular rho even though inverse- and determinant-based NTS density formulas require positive definiteness. ISSUE-001 instead identifies an incorrect scalar factor in a variance formula and repairs that factor; it does not diagnose the undefinedness caused by singular rho or the missing positive-definite premise.
